rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes line 55 from '// Unroll by 4 for better instruction-level parallelism' to '// Unroll by 5 for better instruction-level parallelism'. This is purely a comment change. The actual loop logic 'for (; dim_idx >= 3; dim_idx -= 4)' remains unchanged in both versions. Comments are ignored by the C++ compiler, so the compiled CUDA kernel bytecode is identical.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation survives all testing because it only modifies a comment in the CUDA source code, not actual executable logic. The mutation tool identified the digit '4' in the comment text '// Unroll by 4 for better instruction-level parallelism' as a numeric constant and changed it to '5'. However, since this text follows '//' (C++ single-line comment delimiter), it has zero effect on compilation. The actual loop implementing the unroll (`for (; dim_idx >= 3; dim_idx -= 4)`) processes exactly 4 elements per iteration in both versions. Both versions compile to identical machine code, which is why Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise identical outputs across 112 rounds with various stress patterns.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is truly unkillable under any input configuration. The mutation affects only comment text, not executable code. Both the original and mutant produce identical compiled kernels, making any value-level test impossible.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should implement comment detection to exclude mutations inside C/C++/Python comments. The const_perturb operator should validate that targeted numeric literals are in executable code contexts, not in comments, string literals, or documentation. This would eliminate false-positive 'surviving mutants' that are actually equivalent due to being non-executable.
